new_theme: MODIFY L1 (test): add automatic gain control to a burst recording. A complex 1.2 kHz tone (amplitude 0.5, 48 kHz) times a repeating Vector Source envelope (4000 x 0.1, 4000 x 3.0) -> rx.dat, i.e. bursts at 0.05 and 1.5; the user asks for AGC so every burst has RMS 1.0 +-10 % from 240 samples (5 ms) after each level change, keeping the 1.2 kHz tone and the sources. Reference: analog_agc_xx rate 0.3. v2 signatures: start data_source|mix (test), reference agc|data_source|mix (test); cluster_id chain:agc|data_source|mix.

accepted.change: Applies to the new content in its new form: the instruction's 'do not change the Signal Source or the Vector Source, and keep the envelope multiplying the tone' is enforced by graph checks (block_present with the sources' parameters, path tone -> File Sink, group p2p), and 'add automatic gain control' by a path from the Vector Source to a File Sink through an AGC / AGC2 / AGC3 / Feed-Forward AGC / Divide / Embedded Python block (group f2p). Mutants caught only by these checks: source amplitude 1.0 and a flattened envelope '[1.0]' (both pass every signal check). The values-only rule no longer applies (the item is modify, plan R6).
Same as item-quality/F1; a bypassed AGC (the eval plan's 'missing block' mutation) is in the mutation set and is killed (rms and the AGC path check).

Lesson applied: the stated 'keep the 1.2 kHz tone' is checked in every stretch by peak_freq (+1.2 kHz within 1 %) and band_fraction (>= 99 % within 50 Hz), on 3760-sample windows of exactly 94 periods (no leakage). No swing bound is stated, so none is checked.
Resolved by the re-theme: the item leaves the shared cell filter|tone (gbf-test-10 keeps it) and no longer overlaps the DAC-tone items gbf-test-04/-12; new cell agc|data_source|mix is unique.

notes: Deviations from the fix-plan theme, with evidence (GNU Radio simulation, scratch): (1) settling 5 ms instead of 1 ms - analog_agc_xx updates gain += rate*(ref - |out|), so its time constant is 1/(rate*level); with a 29.5 dB step it settles the weak bursts in >= ~74 samples at the largest stable rates and diverges at rate >= 0.8, so 1 ms would reject the canonical AGC block. (2) A whole-stretch RMS would not see slow settling (rate 0.1 scores 0.986), so each stretch has a separate RMS check over the first 240 samples after the settling time (rate 0.1 scores 0.836 and is a near-miss mutant). (3) Tone 1.2 kHz / amplitude 0.5 with envelope 0.1 / 3.0 (same 0.05 / 1.5 burst levels as planned) because 1 kHz / 1 are catalog defaults that the compact form drops, which a block_present params check cannot name. Accepted designs verified: AGC rates 0.15-0.7, AGC2, AGC3 (incl. 0.5/0.5), Feed-Forward AGC 48 and 200 samples (RMS 0.929: its magnitude estimate is approximate), magnitude/moving-average/Divide normaliser (signature data_source|divide|envelope|filter|mix, test). Known limits in review.notes: dividing by a copy of the known envelope passes; only the first 240 samples after settling and the rest of each stretch are measured.
